claims.text: An actively learned moment tensor potential trained on ab initio high-temperature liquid snapshots can serve as a thermodynamic-integration reference for CoCrFeMnNi near melting.
The MTP reference will be superior to TOR-TILD's EAM references for both solid and liquid states.
The MTP will improve reference-target phase-space overlap.
The MTP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Equimolar CoCrFeMnNi has a melting temperature near 1700 K.
An on-the-fly active-learning MTP can be trained using ab initio MD configurations sampled from both the liquid and solid phases.
The proposed method applies to near-equiatomic multicomponent HEAs containing at least five elements, with each elemental fraction greater than 0.15.
The applicable temperature range is 1400–2000 K, corresponding to approximately ±300 K around the stated melting temperature.
The MTP can capture high-order many-body and multi-element interactions in disordered atomic configurations.
Force matching to a diverse set of ab initio snapshots will make the MTP span more of the target ab initio configuration space than an EAM reference.
Broader coverage of the ab initio configuration space will increase overlap between the MTP reference ensemble and the target ensemble.
Greater reference-target ensemble overlap will reduce the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The expected path-mismatch reduction is approximately 30–60%.
The MTP is expected to yield a path mismatch of approximately 4–7 meV/atom.
TOR-TILD's EAM references exhibit approximately 10 meV/atom path mismatch for liquid and solid CoCrFeMnNi near its melting temperature.
The method may not work for alloys with strong chemical ordering or phase-separation tendencies.
Training-set coverage and extrapolation errors create approximately ±20% uncertainty in the predicted reduction.
Failure to achieve at least a 30% path-mismatch reduction relative to the EAM reference is designated as the decisive falsification outcome.

contradictions.description: The boundary broadly states applicability to equimolar HEAs with at least five elements, whereas the condition that every element exceed 0.15 atomic fraction makes equimolar systems with seven or more elements impossible and therefore does not support unrestricted applicability to all systems with at least five elements.
